content.text:
I built the chart in `index.html`. It renders without errors or warnings. In short, no: once aligned on their release dates, releases fall into two distinct life-cycle shapes.

- **Development** looks about the same for every release, roughly 6 months (median).
- **Interim releases** get 9–19 months of standard support, and exactly 9 months for every one since 2013. Nothing comes after that.
- **LTS releases** get 3.0–5.1 years of standard support. Older ones add extended server support; newer ones add ESM and then the legacy add-on, reaching up to 15 years after release.

The chart has two panels on the same x-axis, LTS on top and interim below. Every number in the caption is calculated from the CSV when the page loads.

```
REPORT
deliverable: index.html
requirements:
  R1: done - one row per release labelled by version, sorted by release date within each group
  R2: done - x = years relative to own release date (0 = release); unit in axis title
  R3: done - dev/standard/extended server/ESM/legacy bars, own colours, legend; missing phases skipped
  R4: done - created = open circle, release = black diamond at 0
  R5: done - separate LTS and interim panels sharing one x scale; LTS labels in bold
  R6: done - title plus caption whose numbers are computed from the data
assumptions:
  - Years = days / 365.25.
  - ESM starts at the later of eol and eol-server (end of the previous phase).
  - Extended server support only drawn when eol-server > eol (true only for 6.06, 8.04, 10.04).
  - "Planned" = after the viewer's current date; those parts are drawn in a lighter shade.
  - Missing trailing CSV fields (d3 parses them as "") are treated as "no date".
limitations:
  - Within-panel order is by release date; the two groups are not interleaved in one list.
  - Planned/past shading depends on the date the page is opened.
  - Hover tooltips (exact dates) are SVG <title> elements, not visible in the static render.
```
